definition: Circulate means to move around through a group or from person to person — the way news spreads, a host works a room, or blood makes its rounds.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word circulate. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know circulate should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Within an hour of the announcement, three rival versions of the story were circulating through the dorm, each more dramatic than the last.
Seep is weaker than circulate: news that seeps escapes slowly at the edges, a detail here and there, while news that circulates is actively passed along, making the full rounds of the group.
Saturate is stronger than circulate: a story that circulates is making its rounds, but a story that saturates has soaked every channel until no one in town could possibly have missed it.

Spread is the broadest word for reaching more people or covering more ground, by any means at all. Circulate specifies the route: the thing travels through a group, passed from person to person or making its rounds along a loop.

Disseminate is deliberate, top-down scattering — an office disseminates guidelines outward to a list of recipients. Circulate moves sideways and often on its own: the members themselves pass the memo, the rumor, the petition around the circle.

The airport shuttle takes a circuitous route to the terminal, so leave yourself twenty extra minutes.
Circulate means to move around through a group or from person to person — the way news spreads, a host works a room, or blood makes its rounds.
The petition to save the corner mural circulated through the neighborhood for two weeks — passed across fences, left on café counters, forwarded to cousins — until nearly every block had signed it.
Nothing was announced from a stage and no office mailed it out: the page moved hand to hand, each signer passing it along to the next.
That person-to-person travel through a group is what circulate describes — and it is why the same verb names what blood does, moving continuously along its circuit.
Circulate is the neutral verb for information on the move: memos, rumors, petitions, and hosts at their own parties all circulate.

Broadcast fires one message at everyone simultaneously; disseminate pushes material outward on purpose; circulate lets it travel the loop, passed along by the group itself — which is why the word so often carries a hint of the unofficial.

The mint can print a bill, but it cannot make one circulate.
A crisp twenty might sit in a drawer for a year; a worn one seems never to rest.
Economists track sample bills the way biologists tag birds, logging each store, wallet, and church plate a note passes through.
One tagged twenty crossed the county eleven times in a summer, moving hand to hand without ever entering a bank.
Money, the study concluded, is healthiest when it keeps moving through many hands — and a bill that stops moving might as well not exist.
